nuggets.title: One movie counted as dozens of sessions

scenario.symptoms: Analytics shows average session length of 4 minutes for a 2-hour film. Heartbeat events every 30s create a new session whenever mobile OS pauses the app briefly.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Sessionization uses a rigid 5-minute inactivity gap with no merge logic for background audio or casting handoffs.

incident.headline: Aggressive inactivity timeout fragments continuous viewing into many sessions

agenda.goal: Define playback sessions that match real viewing behavior.
agenda.opener: A single movie became 30 sessions—how should session boundaries be defined?

evidence.strong: Tune gap by content type, merge on same content id, handle cast/background states, and use explicit session end events.
evidence.adequate: Increase timeout globally without content-aware rules.
evidence.weak: Every app open is a new session regardless of playback.

misconceptions.pattern: One global inactivity gap for all surfaces.
misconceptions.challenge: Background audio may pause heartbeats—is that a new session?

probes: What events mark session start vs continuation?
How do you sessionize offline downloads playing later?
hints: Same content + user + device may continue one session.
agenda.referenceFix: Use content-aware timeouts, continue sessions across brief gaps on same asset, emit session_end on stop, and validate against known runtime distributions.

scenario.symptoms: Reported watch minutes exceed available content duration by 3x for binge watchers. Scrubbing backward generates overlapping progress events summed naively.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Watch time aggregator sums delta position without capping at content length or deduping overlapping intervals.

incident.headline: Naive delta summing double-counts time when users seek backward

agenda.goal: Compute accurate unique watch time per user and asset.
agenda.opener: Watch minutes exceed movie length—what is wrong with the aggregation logic?

evidence.strong: Interval merge on timeline, cap at asset duration, heartbeat max jump, and QoE-validated playhead monotonic segments.

probes: How do you count rewatched segments?
What if heartbeats arrive out of order?
hints: Think interval coverage on a timeline.
Rewatch may count separately if product requires.
agenda.referenceFix: Build merged intervals per session capped to content runtime, discard out-of-order noise, and document whether rewatches add to unique watch time.

nuggets.title: Late mobile events corrupt session order

scenario.symptoms: Session funnels show impossible sequences: ‘complete’ before ‘start’. Devices offline for hours upload buffered events that land out of order in the stream processor.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Flink job uses processing time windows without event-time watermarks or client timestamps.

incident.headline: Processing-time sessionization misorders late-arriving playback events

agenda.goal: Sessionize using event time with tolerance for offline buffering.
agenda.opener: Sessions show end before start after offline sync—how should the pipeline handle late events?

evidence.strong: Event-time watermarks, client event timestamps, allowed lateness, and idempotent upserts keyed by session id.
evidence.adequate: Sort batch replay only without streaming watermarks.

probes: How long should allowed lateness be for mobile offline?
What id keys tie events to one session?
agenda.referenceFix: Use client event timestamps with watermarks and allowed lateness, reorder within session key, and upsert session state idempotently when late events arrive.
